verdict.rationale: Homebrew documents third-party taps as its extension mechanism. `brew tap` adds repositories that supply formulae, casks and external commands from GitHub or any Git URL, and the docs cover fully qualified tap selection, per-item trust, untapping, repair, and tap-provided bottles. Community users confirm hosting their own taps, though hosting one requires a git server rather than a static host. Missing for 10: in-depth evidence on authoring external commands (plugin-style subcommands); tap hosting is limited to git-protocol servers rather than simple static/CDN hosting.

support.subject: As a developer, I can extend the manager through third-party taps, overlays, plugins, or backends

citations.quote: The `brew tap` command adds repositories that Homebrew can use for formulae, casks and external commands.
The one-argument form assumes a repository on GitHub, while the two-argument form accepts any URL supported by Git.
`brew tap <user>/<repository>` clones `https://github.com/<user>/homebrew-<repository>` into Homebrew’s tap directory.
Use the fully qualified name to select the formula from a particular tap
This may be useful for taps that wish to provide bottles for their formulae or cater to a non-default HOMEBREW_CELLAR.
